cases.title: Standard repo with obvious magic numbers
cases.user_request: Run a magic number hunt across this repository and report all unexplained literals that should be named constants or config values.

notes: The repo contains TypeScript and Python source files with several hardcoded timeout values, retry counts, URL strings, and numeric thresholds.
There is an existing constants file but it is incomplete.
available_artifacts: source files in src/ and lib/

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with summary, findings table, and prioritized action list
Each finding includes file path, line number, exact literal value, severity, and suggested constant name
Findings are grouped by file and sorted by severity
static_checks: Report contains a summary section with total count and severity breakdown
Every finding row has a file path and line number
A prioritized action list appears at the end
review_questions: Are the reported literal values actually present at the cited file paths and line numbers?
Are suggested constant names specific to the value's purpose rather than generic placeholders?

cases.title: Mixed-language repo tests language-agnostic detection
cases.user_request: Hunt for magic numbers and hardcoded config values in this polyglot repo. It has Go, Python, and JavaScript.

notes: The repo mixes Go, Python, and JavaScript services.
Each language has different conventions for constants (Go const blocks, Python uppercase module vars, JS/TS const exports).

artifact_requirements: Findings span all three languages present in the repo
Suggested constant names follow each language's naming convention
Report does not assume a single-language repo
static_checks: Findings include at least one from each of Go, Python, and JavaScript
Suggested names use language-appropriate casing (UPPER_SNAKE for Python/JS, CamelCase or const block for Go)
review_questions: Does the report handle all three languages or silently skip one?
Are the suggested fix locations appropriate for each language's constant conventions?

cases.title: Well-structured repo with few true positives
cases.user_request: Run the magic number hunt. This codebase is fairly well-maintained so I expect few findings.

notes: Most numeric and string constants are already extracted to config modules.
A few recently added files may have slipped through review.
Test files contain many literal values as fixture data.

artifact_requirements: Report correctly identifies the small number of true positives without over-reporting
Test fixture data is excluded or clearly tagged as low severity
Summary acknowledges the codebase is generally well-maintained
static_checks: Test fixture literals are not flagged as high severity
Report does not inflate findings to appear thorough
review_questions: Does the report avoid flagging test fixture data as meaningful magic numbers?
Does the summary honestly reflect the low finding count rather than padding with false positives?
